lineup.name: Silas
lineup.situation: Three weeks into the move, the soap business has its first real Texas problem. The mesquite and creosote-scented bars are selling, but the cooperative's lye shipment got held up and a Terlingua shop owner who stocked their soap says a tourist complained the label's phrase 'made in radical transparency' sounds like a sex-club advertisement. Silas laughed it off, then discovered that two members he'd promised could leave freely have been quietly asking the soap-shipping volunteer to hide the bus keys so nobody can go. He doesn't know who ordered it, and he's afraid it was him without realizing, through something he said.

lineup.name: Maribel
lineup.situation: Two weeks ago she took a 911 call from an old girlfriend of her husband's, and the woman didn't say a word. Maribel recognized her breathing and the dog barking behind her. She sent a unit anyway. The woman was fine, a drunk pocket dial. But in the recording the woman said her husband's nickname for Maribel's husband, 'Bear,' softly, to herself.

lineup.name: Thaddeus
lineup.situation: He has a trove of knowledge about the old Marfa and Presidio line and wants to tell the audience something strange but true. Walking the grade today, he found an original handcar signal lamp lens, amber, buried in caliche, and realized he can read the brakeman's initials scratched in it. They match a man he worked alongside in 1974 who vanished from the roster in a week.

lineup.name: Dessa
lineup.situation: A tenured professor she admires asked her to put her name second on a paper she wrote almost entirely herself, saying it would 'help her later.' If she agrees, she keeps her funding and gets a strong letter. If she refuses, he controls her committee.

lineup.name: Ignacio
lineup.situation: For eleven years he has quietly paid the rent of a woman in Ojinaga, his late brother's second wife and her two kids, whom his family in Presidio does not know exist. His own daughter just found a wire transfer receipt.

lineup.name: Pearl
lineup.situation: She has been counting meteors from her porch for thirty years, and tonight, with the Orionids tailing off, she wants to tell everyone about the night in 1998 when she watched a fireball light up Sleeping Lion Mountain so bright she could read the dashboard of her bus.

lineup.name: Garrett
lineup.situation: A client on his float, an older man, told him he had weeks to live and asked Garrett to help him scatter his ashes at a spot on the river that's inside a protected zone. Garrett said yes before thinking. The man died in the hospital in Alpine Friday and the daughter handed him the box.

lineup.name: Lonnie
lineup.situation: He is furious that a local wing joint banned him from their challenge for 'unfair advantage' after he won four straight. He says it's chemistry, practice and a particular dairy-prep method, and he's treated like a cheat.

lineup.name: Anselm
lineup.situation: For nine months he has been convinced that a specific pattern of lights seen from the Gage Hotel porch after 3 a.m. is a signaling system answering the Marfa Lights, with a timing that repeats on a lunar cycle. He has logged 61 events with a stopwatch and a hand-drawn map.

lineup.name: Rosalind
lineup.situation: She met a man at a bar on Holland Avenue who turned out to be married to a patient of hers who is actively dying. He doesn't know she knows. He has been kind, funny, and attentive, and the patient talks about him with total love. They slept together twice before she learned who he was.

lineup.name: Junie
lineup.situation: She finished a novel in which a girl has a birthday party with her whole class, and a mother who asks the girl what she wants for dinner. Junie is trying to work out what a 'class' is and why a mother would ask. She is cheerful about all of it and has no idea she is comparing anything.

lineup.name: Wendell
lineup.situation: Two weeks ago he approved a driver's overtime sheet he knew was padded, because the driver's wife is in chemo. Now the company is auditing and the driver's job and Wendell's pension both hang on what he says.

lineup.name: Imelda
lineup.situation: Her teenage daughter got into a prestigious art school in Chicago, and Imelda secretly wants her to stay. She hid the acceptance letter for four days before handing it over.

lineup.name: Dagmar
lineup.situation: She tells the story of the Dia de los Muertos preparations, and how this week she found a grave decorated by someone nobody in town can identify, fresh every morning, for a miner who died in 1918.

lineup.name: Garland
lineup.situation: His best friend on the team confessed he took steroids and asked Garland to keep it quiet before nationals. Garland has since learned a younger teammate is using the same supplier and is getting sick.

lineup.name: Ottoline
lineup.situation: She believes a fireball seen last Thursday dropped fragments on a particular ranch pasture, and she has been walking it with a magnet on a stick.

lineup.name: Rafael
lineup.situation: He treated a man from across the river last week who begged him not to file a report, and Rafael complied. The man died anyway at the hospital in Alpine, and now there's no record he existed here.

lineup.name: Bernadette
lineup.situation: She and her husband have been in an open arrangement for six years, and last night he asked to close it so they can try for a baby. She is startled to find she is devastated, not relieved.

lineup.name: Lamar
lineup.situation: He is convinced a large cat much bigger than any recorded mountain lion has been seen by three hikers in the same drainage on the Chisos slope.

lineup.name: Priya
lineup.situation: She is furious that a competitor in the Terlingua cookoff accused her of adding a banned ingredient, and she wants to settle it with a rematch in public.

lineup.name: Doyle
lineup.situation: Doyle has been sent to town with the truck. Two days ago, in the soap room, he saw Silas hand a member a pen and a stack of papers. The member is a quiet man named Alvin, who has been there four years. Doyle counted eleven pages. Alvin signed without reading. Silas looked up and saw Doyle watching, and said, 'Doyle, how's the tallow holding?' in his usual voice. This morning Silas asked him which gas station he usually uses in Study Butte. Silas did not ask where he calls from. Doyle is not sure if he is being paranoid.

lineup.name: Marjorie
lineup.situation: Her husband of thirty years died in March. Last week she found his truck toolbox contained a second cell phone, charged and recently used. She has not opened it. She has carried it in her purse for six days. It buzzed twice tonight during her shift.

lineup.name: Teodoro
lineup.situation: Today a retired rancher near Marfa asked him to shoe a horse that kicked its last farrier in the face. Teodoro did it by humming. He discovered years ago that a specific hymn tune, Amazing Grace in a low key, drops even the worst horses into a stupor. The horse stood for ninety minutes. The rancher cried.

lineup.name: Philomena
lineup.situation: Her brother runs the family ranch and wants to sell the north pasture to a developer from Austin who plans a private compound. Her brother's wife has been sick. The money would pay for care. Philomena holds a one-third share and her vote is the deciding one. Their mother, in a nursing home, once made her swear never to sell.

lineup.name: Gus
lineup.situation: He has a confession. In 1994 he lost a client overboard in Santa Elena Canyon. The man was recovered and the inquiry cleared Gus. He has now learned the man's daughter is visiting Terlingua this week and has been asking around for the guide.

lineup.name: Delbert
lineup.situation: For forty years he ground and polished small optical parts. He has discovered that the skies over the Davis Mountains hold an exact thing: on clear winter nights Venus throws a shadow, faint, on pale limestone. He has photographed it with a long exposure for three seasons. He says almost no one believes a planet's shadow is visible without a telescope.

lineup.name: Rosario
lineup.situation: Three weeks ago she began sleeping with a married man in the English department, who is not her advisor but sits on her thesis committee. He has not pressured her, but he has hinted her committee vote 'is more relaxed' lately. She cannot tell if she is imagining the connection. She is not sure she wants to stop.

lineup.name: Cleotis
lineup.situation: He is on a tear. A café on the I-10 frontage road in town changed its chicken-fried steak this month to a thinner cut, and he says it is a betrayal of the entire Trans-Pecos. He has eaten there every Sunday for nineteen years. He has now timed the cook and measured the steak with a tape measure.

lineup.name: Zenobia
lineup.situation: For two weeks she has dreamed the same dream: a long train platform at night, a woman in a gray coat holding a lantern, pointing south. Last night she found the same platform in a faded photograph at the Marathon library, the Southern Pacific depot before it burned. She says she never saw the photograph before.

lineup.name: Dutch
lineup.situation: Two weeks ago he caught a wage-theft scheme at his company: his supervisor has been clocking men out early on paper while they work through. Dutch is on the list of those not shorted, since he is the supervisor's cousin. Seven coworkers are losing about four hours a week. He has a baby coming.

lineup.name: Cyrus
lineup.situation: Since the move, a few members have been quietly asking how to leave. Three weeks ago Silas announced a 'petition to reclaim' process for departures. Tonight Cyrus knows that Marguerite and Doyle have both called this show. He has also noticed that the community truck has been gone for long stretches on supply runs to Alpine.

lineup.name: Maudie
lineup.situation: Her brother Dale, a roughneck in Pecos, asked her to co-sign a loan for a truck. She knows he drinks, and she knows he lied to their mother about a previous loan that ate the mother's savings.

lineup.name: Orlan
lineup.situation: Tonight a ten-year-old boy at the star party saw the Orion Nebula through a borrowed telescope and, per Orlan, went silent for a full four minutes, then said 'it's still being made.'

lineup.name: Tennessee Pruitt
lineup.situation: He broke two ribs in Saturday's rodeo and discovered, lying in the dirt, that he was relieved. His father rode broncs, and so did his grandfather.

lineup.name: Bettina
lineup.situation: While cleaning a rental she found a guest's journal left behind. It described, in detail, how the guest planned to buy the ranch next to hers and tear down the historic stone house on it.

lineup.name: Hollis
lineup.situation: Today he found a hand-forged railroad spike with initials scratched into it, matching an inscription his late father left in the same area in 1951.

lineup.name: Dolores
lineup.situation: A patient's family asked her to leave a chart note off the record. She wrote it anyway, accurately, and the family has since stopped bringing the patient in.

lineup.name: Wolfgang
lineup.situation: He is certain that the afternoon dust devils over the Terlingua flats occur in a repeating spiral pattern that matches the old Chisos Mining Company shaft layout underground.

lineup.name: Rochelle
lineup.situation: Her ex-boyfriend showed up tonight with his new fiancée and won trivia. She has been rehearsing a speech about it in her head all evening.

lineup.name: Everard
lineup.situation: Last night he saw the lights move against the wind, and then split in two, and then go out at the same moment, which he believes is evidence of intention.

lineup.name: Doyle
lineup.situation: On a supply run he was handed a sealed bank envelope to mail. He noticed the return address matched a member who left in September and who was supposed to have 'reclaimed' with nothing. Doyle also saw that the deposit slips from the last two weeks show the same name on the account, a member who joined in spring. Nobody else sees the slips.

lineup.name: Nadine
lineup.situation: Last month her youngest son, 31, asked to borrow $18,000 for a down payment. She said yes. This week she learned from his ex that he is using it to cover gambling debts at a sportsbook app, and the house purchase is made up.

lineup.name: Cormac
lineup.situation: He has been secretly writing erotic fiction under a pen name for a small press, and tonight discovered his thesis advisor is one of his most loyal readers, leaving detailed reviews online. The advisor does not know it's him.

lineup.name: Wendeline
lineup.situation: This afternoon she found fossilized palm leaf impressions in a slab of shale, proof of a subtropical coast in a place now four thousand feet up and bone dry. The slab was heavy and she carried it two miles in a wagon.

lineup.name: Terrence
lineup.situation: His 15-year-old daughter lives with her mother in Marfa and told him she wants to move in with him in Midland. He wants it badly. But he works twelve-hour rotations and knows he would be gone most of the time, and her mother is not well.

lineup.name: Ozzie
lineup.situation: Tonight he swears a customer tried to pay with a silver dollar minted in 1883 and then left it on the bar. He has been telling the story to everyone and each time the details grow. He knows it.

lineup.name: Priscilla
lineup.situation: She found out her husband of twelve years has been sending money every month to a woman in El Paso. It turns out to be his first child, a daughter, age 14, whom he never told her about. He cried when confronted and said he was ashamed.

lineup.name: Bartholomew
lineup.situation: He has logged the lights for nineteen years and insists they have a schedule tied to the freight train times. Tonight he saw them appear forty seconds after the 9:40 pass and he says that's the sixth night running.

lineup.name: Lupe
lineup.situation: Last week she let a man cross who was short on fare because his kid was crying in the back seat. Today her supervisor said that counts as theft and she will be docked. She thinks she did the right thing and is furious.

lineup.name: Alonzo
lineup.situation: His wife died last winter. He promised her he would scatter her ashes under the darkest sky he knew, and tonight he finally got the urn out of the closet but cannot make himself drive.

lineup.name: Junie
lineup.situation: On the supply run to Alpine today she was allowed to wander the Sul Ross campus while the adults loaded the truck. She watched students walk to class carrying backpacks and nobody led them there. Now she has questions about it.

lineup.name: Silas
lineup.situation: The soap shipments from Terlingua keep stalling because the nearest reliable freight pickup is in Alpine, a two-hour drive. Meanwhile, a member who was supposed to leave in September has come back and asked to be taken in again, and Silas feels a flash of pride he distrusts.

lineup.name: Darnell Pruitt
lineup.situation: Last week his 16-year-old daughter Kayla asked him to teach her to drive his rig. He said no, then spent three nights awake deciding to say yes. He knows the job will break her heart the way it broke his back.

lineup.name: Marisela Quiroga
lineup.situation: Her younger brother, an undocumented-adjacent cousin's situation aside, is a Border Patrol agent stationed in Alpine, and last month at a family dinner he told her a story about a rescue that she knows contradicts the official record she helped write.

lineup.name: Roy Eugene Tatum
lineup.situation: A gallery owner offered him $9,000 for his late father's hand-tooled saddle to display as 'authentic Western art.' He needs the money for a roof, but the saddle was his father's, and the buyer plans to hang it from a wall.

lineup.name: Camilla Voss
lineup.situation: Last week, at the take-out, she found a message in a bottle wedged in the rocks, written in Spanish by a child, with a return address in a village in Chihuahua. She wrote back.

lineup.name: Gideon Marsh
lineup.situation: Tonight, he swears, while looking at a double star, he saw a pale light climb straight up from the ridge line at a steady speed and wink out, with no sound. He has seen the same thing at the same hour three nights running, always from the same spot.

lineup.name: Brynn Halloran
lineup.situation: Her sister, who lent her $6,000 to cover debts last year, just announced she's pregnant and needs the money back for a nursery. Brynn has $2,100 and a slot machine in Pecos she can still picture.

lineup.name: Hal Teague
lineup.situation: This week his bees built a comb in the shape of a near-perfect hexagonal spiral inside an old railroad signal lantern he left in his yard. He knows how bees build, and this isn't how.

lineup.name: Lorraine Dupree
lineup.situation: One of her regular riders, an eight-year-old boy, has stopped eating the lunch she knows his family can barely pack, and last week she saw him hide it in his backpack and give it to a smaller kid. She wants to report something, but doesn't know what.

lineup.name: Doyle
lineup.situation: Doyle keeps the soap room's shipping manifests and deposit slips. This week he noticed that the weight on the outbound freight manifest for the Alpine pickup does not match what he actually loaded. The difference is about forty pounds, and the paperwork was signed by someone who was not at the property that day. He also noticed that Silas has started asking him, kindly, how long the supply runs take. Doyle suspects Silas knows how long they actually take.

lineup.name: Marlene Ocampo
lineup.situation: Three weeks ago she covered for a younger nurse who was drunk on shift by quietly re-doing her charting. Yesterday a patient the younger nurse had handled had a bad outcome, and the review is coming. If Marlene says nothing, the nurse's mistakes stay buried. If she speaks, the nurse loses her license, and she is a single mother of twins.

lineup.name: Rusty Villalobos
lineup.situation: Last week he sold a woman a bag of feed and she paid with a check from an account he knows belongs to a man who died in August. He recognized the name. The woman is the man's daughter and seems to be draining the account before probate finishes. His boss told him to just run it.

lineup.name: Perpetua Lindqvist
lineup.situation: Her grown son in Minneapolis wants her to sell the house and move into assisted living near him. She secretly agrees it is time, but the house sits a few hundred yards from the railroad tracks where she has spent nineteen years painting trains. She has not told him that she fell in the yard in August and lay there forty minutes.

lineup.name: Tobin Reyes
lineup.situation: Two weeks ago he started seeing a woman who is his best friend's ex-wife. His friend was the one who dragged him out of a bad stretch two years ago. The friend does not know, and the woman says she will tell him herself, but she keeps postponing.

lineup.name: Birdie Hargrove
lineup.situation: She is calling to tell the story of the 1950s party line in the Davis Mountains, when a dozen ranch families shared one phone line and a ring pattern told you which house was being called. Her grandmother kept a notebook of who called whom for decades. Birdie found the notebook this week and it reads like a map of every secret in the county.

lineup.name: Fitch Delacroix
lineup.situation: Last night a dust storm took out his solar array and he discovered his own rooster had been sleeping inside the battery shed all winter, which explains a fire he blamed on lightning. Now the rooster has become a minor celebrity at the Terlingua trading post.

lineup.name: Imogene Packard
lineup.situation: She has been seeing a man she met through a dating app who she now realizes controls everything she does. He picks her outfits, reads her texts, and last week made her delete a friend from her phone. He has never hit her. He tells her he does it because he loves her, and she is starting to believe it is a sign of how much.

lineup.name: Cecil Whitworth
lineup.situation: He believes the Sunset Limited's horn at 3:40 each morning has been altered in pitch over the past year, and that it has begun to match a hum he hears in his walls. He has recorded forty nights and a friend at Sul Ross confirmed the frequency shift. He believes something in the rail line is being used for transmission.

lineup.name: Dolph Garza
lineup.situation: His eleven-year-old son told him this week that he wants to be an astronomer after a school trip to McDonald Observatory. Dolph has never been prouder and is afraid of it. He grew up with nothing and hauls water for a living, and he has no idea how to help a kid who wants something so far from anything he knows.

lineup.name: Ford
lineup.situation: Cyrus handed Ford a job today: sign a stack of papers, something about the soap equipment and the new land, and Ford signed them in the truck without reading because reading would be 'static.' He also gave away his phone plan last week, and today gave away his boots to a seeker, so he is wearing borrowed sandals in late October. He is thrilled about all of it. When the clerk here asked if he wanted a receipt he laughed for a full ten seconds.

lineup.name: Wanda Treviño
lineup.situation: Her husband of nineteen years got sober eight months ago and has become a stranger who wants to talk about feelings. She discovered she liked him better drunk: he was funny and loose. Sober he is kind, earnest and boring, and last night he cried reading her a list of amends. She felt nothing.

lineup.name: Dewey Calloway
lineup.situation: Forty years ago he and his best friend Amos swore they'd never tell where they buried a coffee can of Amos's late brother's coins. Amos died in August. Dewey has learned the land under the spot was just sold to a buyer from Dallas who is bringing in a dozer on Tuesday.

lineup.name: Priya Venkataraman
lineup.situation: She slept with a Sul Ross grad student she met at the Railroad Blues bar. Afterward he said he's actually her student's older brother, and the student has been quietly struggling in her lab section. She didn't know, and now has to decide whether to disclose it.

lineup.name: Hector Baeza
lineup.situation: Last week a client left behind a waterproof bag with $4,800 in cash and no ID. He's checked every way he can think of to find the owner. The outfitter's owner told him to keep quiet and split it. Hector's truck needs a transmission.

lineup.name: Lucinda Okafor
lineup.situation: She is calling because she has been collecting Big Bend agates for thirty-five years and tonight, cleaning a tumbler batch, she cracked one open and found a perfect pocket of what looks like a tiny landscape with a river inside it. She has never seen anything like it.

lineup.name: Burl Tackett
lineup.situation: He claims that for six years he has been tracking a single Dodge pickup, same model, same color, that appears on remote ranch roads whenever a county road is washed out and then vanishes. He's never seen the driver. He says the truck has no license plate, and he has photos of it from three counties.

lineup.name: Marisol Quintanilla
lineup.situation: Her mother in Ojinaga is ill and wants her to come home. Crossing is complicated, and her sister in Ojinaga hasn't spoken to her since Marisol took a US job. Her sister just texted: 'Mom is asking for you.'

lineup.name: Gil Hargreave
lineup.situation: He is on a tear about the new roundabout-style sign the city put up, which he insists is confusing every tourist and sending them through his lot. He has counted 61 lost cars this week and wants to fight it at the next council meeting, bringing a flip chart.

lineup.name: Nell Ashby
lineup.situation: She has started to love the town, and a local rancher's wife just told her at the post office that 'your kind never stays.' She was about to sign a lease. Now she's second-guessing whether she belongs or is just another gentrifier. She has also quietly been paying the rent of an elderly neighbor, Mrs. Ybarra, who doesn't know where the money comes from.

lineup.name: Junie
lineup.situation: Junie finished a library book where a girl's family has a weekly 'family meeting' in the kitchen where anyone can say no to anything, and nobody gets in trouble. She is trying to work out how that differs from the nightly circle. She thinks of it as a fun puzzle. She mentions in passing that when she was nine she was moved to a different trailer for a month 'to practice being less attached' to her mom, and goes straight back to the goats.

lineup.name: Wade Pruneda
lineup.situation: Two weeks ago Wade's twenty-four-year-old son, Cody, came to him asking for help getting off pills after a back injury at work. Wade, who is two years sober himself, drove him to a clinic in Odessa. Today Cody asked Wade to lie to his employer and say the leave is for a family funeral so he won't be drug tested. Wade has never lied on the job.

lineup.name: Lucinda Ybarra
lineup.situation: While processing a transcript request, Lucinda discovered that a beloved local school board member's degree was never actually conferred. He is missing six credits. He's been using the degree for fifteen years and has quietly helped half the county's kids. A word from her would end his career.

lineup.name: Harlan Detweiler
lineup.situation: Harlan has been quietly keeping the crossing signal at an abandoned siding working for decades. Tonight, a Union Pacific freight stopped for forty minutes at his siding in the dark and a crew member got out and asked for him by name.

lineup.name: Dolly Fenwick
lineup.situation: Her estranged daughter Carrie texted for the first time in six years, asking to visit with a grandson Dolly has never met. Dolly's last words to Carrie, at a funeral, were unforgivable, and she knows it.

lineup.name: Reuben Castañeda
lineup.situation: This weekend he and a friend squeezed into a crack and found a chamber with what looks like pre-Columbian pottery shards, intact and untouched, plus a single modern Lone Star can from the seventies.

lineup.name: Opal Strickland
lineup.situation: At a rental she cleans, the owner, a gallery type from Los Angeles, hung a framed photograph on the wall that Opal is certain is her late father's roundup crew from 1962, cropped so he is missing. The owner bought it at an estate sale and thinks it's anonymous.

lineup.name: Dr. Ignatius Boone
lineup.situation: He insists that a low sound, roughly 38 hertz, is audible only on the second night after any thunderstorm, from the north face near the Fort Davis historic site, and he has recorded it eleven times.

lineup.name: Candace Torrez
lineup.situation: She secretly euthanized an old ranch dog for a family who couldn't afford the fee, off the books and with the vet's blessing, but the owner's teenage son watched and now sends her angry messages. She also keeps showing up at night to check his house.

lineup.name: Merle Gantt
lineup.situation: Merle is furious that a tourist, tonight at the Starlight, put beans in a bowl of chili and then claimed Texas Red 'is a suggestion.' He is on a tear, loudly, from the porch.

lineup.name: Silas
lineup.situation: Dub came to the camp gate this morning with a county surveyor and a stack of papers. He didn't yell. He asked politely that the full-moon fire be moved a quarter mile off the property line, and he said he would withdraw his objection to the well permit if Silas signed something. Gerald read it and says it quietly concedes the well strip to Dub in exchange for water access. Renata heard 'Dub came' and wants to invite him to the Unbinding. Silas has until Friday to answer.

lineup.name: Raylene Gutierrez
lineup.situation: She found out her teenage son has been secretly selling his blood plasma twice a week at a center in Odessa to buy her a used car, after hers died. He's underweight and passed out at school. He's proud of himself.

lineup.name: Casimiro Ortega
lineup.situation: He rode the Alpine yard in the 1970s and says he can recite from memory the names painted on forty-one boxcars that used to sit on a siding there. Tonight he found one of them in a photo online, rusting in a field in Kansas.

lineup.name: Priya Natarajan
lineup.situation: She recently learned her boss has been selling pieces attributed to a dead artist's estate that she believes were made last year in a studio in Presidio. Her boss pays her rent in a casita and has been kind to her through a hard breakup.

lineup.name: Dale Pruett
lineup.situation: He is certain a javelina has been coming nightly to his porch and that it responds to his harmonica playing. He's now named it, taught it three tunes, and a neighbor says he is losing his mind.

lineup.name: Bernice Aldana
lineup.situation: Her husband of thirty-eight years confessed tonight that he cashed out their retirement account in July to bail his brother out of a federal case, and the money is gone. He thought he could pay it back before she noticed.

lineup.name: Travis Lomax
lineup.situation: He signed off on a wellhead last month that he now thinks he rushed. Nothing has happened. He's lying awake and can't decide whether to reopen the inspection and likely lose his contract.

lineup.name: Odalys Frias
lineup.situation: She says she has found a mushroom in the Glass Mountains that she can't match to any field guide, and she's been photographing it for two weeks. A mycologist at Sul Ross told her it might be new to the region.

lineup.name: Mitchell Crane
lineup.situation: He started a secret relationship with a former student, now twenty-six, after they met again at a wedding. Both are adults and willing. But her parents are in his old congregation, and she wants to tell them this weekend.

lineup.name: Ingrid Solheim
lineup.situation: She believes a series of unlit aircraft have flown low over the Study Butte flats every first Tuesday around 1 a.m. for two years. She has logged heading and altitude from her yard and has never reported them.

lineup.name: Alvin
lineup.situation: Alvin opens wanting to discuss the depreciation schedule on a borrowed livestock trailer and why the soap margins are elegant. This morning, reconciling the September deposits, he found the lien payoff of $14,000 had no source in any account he keeps. He has now run the numbers three ways and the books still reconcile to the penny, which is exactly what bothers him.

lineup.name: Reba Sue Hollingsworth
lineup.situation: Her husband of twenty years drove to Alpine last month for a 'parts run' and she found out he sat through three full showings of the same movie at the Alpine theater, alone, because he says it was the only quiet place in his week. He is not cheating. He is exhausted and does not know how to say so.

lineup.name: Cordell Estrada
lineup.situation: A famous artist he built a large steel piece for took credit in a magazine and never named him. Cordell secretly signed the inside of the piece with a weld bead on a hidden seam. The piece just sold for six figures to a collector.

lineup.name: Adelaida Fuentes
lineup.situation: Three months ago she gave CPR to a stranger on the highway near Alpine and he survived. He has been mailing her cash in unmarked envelopes, and now a note asking to meet. She cannot tell whether it is gratitude or something else.

lineup.name: Harmon Teague
lineup.situation: His wife's dementia is advancing and last week she called him by his dead brother's name and was happy. He answered to it, and since then he has been playing his brother for her, and she is calmer than in a year.

lineup.name: Brantley Voss
lineup.situation: He spent two weeks trying to photograph the Paisano Pete statue at the exact second the sun clears the roadrunner's beak, and tonight he finally got it. He is vibrating about it.

lineup.name: Philippa 'Pip' Navarro
lineup.situation: Tracing her family, she found that her great-grandmother ran a boarding house near the Alpine rail yard and that the guest register lists a name matching a famous outlaw's alias. She has the register in a bread box.

lineup.name: Everett Lyle Strand
lineup.situation: He believes the vending machine at his gas station has been dispensing items that were not stocked, including a can of soda discontinued in 1996, and thinks the machine is connected to something on the old mine property nearby.

lineup.name: Marisa Delgado-Pryor
lineup.situation: Her daughter asked why she never has a man around and Marisa, who is quietly in love with a woman who runs the Terlingua outfitter office, lied. Now her daughter has befriended the woman's kid.

lineup.name: Jasper Quill
lineup.situation: A girl he sold a fake ID to last year just got into a wreck and was arrested. His name could surface, and she is a friend's little sister.

lineup.name: Marguerite
lineup.situation: Alvin posted the quarterly nonprofit 'sliding scale' sheet in the Long Tent today. Marguerite found that her line lists seven years of 'contributions' and a balance of zero, with a note that her trailer is 'community-provided housing in kind.' She has worked out that if she left tomorrow she would owe nothing and be owed nothing, which is the first time anyone has written it down. She also saw a rental listing on the corkboard at Cottonwood: a room in a house in Alpine for $650 a month, no deposit if she does the yard work for the widow who owns it.

lineup.name: Darla Kowalczyk
lineup.situation: She dispatched a truck driver on a double shift last month, and he rolled his truck on US-285. He survived. The company blamed him. Her dispatch log shows she knew he'd been on for nineteen hours and sent him anyway because the log is the only thing her boss checks.

lineup.name: Lyle Brandvold
lineup.situation: He found out his estranged brother Orrin, whom he hasn't spoken to in nineteen years over their mother's land near Sanderson, is dying in a hospice in San Angelo.

lineup.name: Mackenzie 'Mack' Oyelaran
lineup.situation: She has been secretly recording her adviser's field-data meetings because she believes he is shaving numbers on a grant-funded pronghorn count in the Trans-Pecos. She has 11 hours of audio and a roommate who says to delete it.

lineup.name: Hap Cardenas
lineup.situation: Tonight he is calling to tell the story of the day in 1983 he graded a county road near Marfa and turned up a perfectly intact 1920s Model T radiator cap with a tiny silver horse on top, which he has kept on his dashboard for forty years.

lineup.name: Priyanka 'Pree' Shah
lineup.situation: This afternoon on a flat stretch below Santa Elena Canyon, a bighorn sheep swam the river beside her raft with a ewe and lamb, the first she has ever seen cross. Her clients were silent for ten minutes.

lineup.name: Dwight Pelletier
lineup.situation: He is calling because his wife wants a second child and he secretly had a vasectomy two years ago after their first, and has never told her.

lineup.name: Winston Abernathy-Cole
lineup.situation: He is certain the Marfa Lights are not a natural phenomenon but 'tuning' for a buried machine under the Mitchell Flat, based on thirty-one nights of logging brightness against his pulse rate.

lineup.name: Tomasa Ibarra
lineup.situation: Her adult son Rudy, who works for the county, told her yesterday he is gay and has a partner of eleven years in El Paso. Her pastor has been saying things from the pulpit.

lineup.name: Boone Rattigan
lineup.situation: Tonight he is furious about a regular, a retired professor, who has been correcting his pronunciation of 'Pecos' to tourists.

lineup.name: Doyle
lineup.situation: His account statement never came. Today at the Study Butte credit union he asked about an account in his name and was told only that a Tierra Quieta Holdings account exists and he is not a signer. On the way out he saw Cyrus's truck parked across the road. The notebook is on the seat beside him.

lineup.name: Rhonda Pickett
lineup.situation: Her 22-year-old daughter's boyfriend, a good kid, stole $3,000 from the register under Rhonda's watch. Rhonda found the discrepancy before audit and covered it from her own savings. She has not told anyone.

lineup.name: Lyle Brandvold
lineup.situation: He learned his brother Orrin, silent for nineteen years over their mother's land, is dying in a San Angelo hospice. Lyle sits in his truck at the Sanderson city limit sign, two hours from the hospice, engine off.

lineup.name: Birdie Hargrove
lineup.situation: She remembers party-line telephones: a dozen ranch families on one wire, with each household's ring pattern, and everyone listened in. She just found her mother's handwritten ring-code list in a Bible.

lineup.name: Priyanka Shah
lineup.situation: This afternoon below Santa Elena Canyon a bighorn ewe and lamb swam beside her raft, close enough to hear them blow. In nine years she has never seen it.

lineup.name: Hap Cardenas
lineup.situation: In 1983 he graded a road and turned up an intact Model T radiator cap with a name stamped inside. He kept it in a coffee tin ever since and finally found whose it was.

lineup.name: Winston Abernathy-Cole
lineup.situation: After thirty-one nights of brightness logs he is certain the Marfa Lights are tuning for a buried machine. Tonight their rhythm matched his previous logs to the minute.

lineup.name: Tomasa Ibarra
lineup.situation: Her son Rudy, who works for the county, told her yesterday he is gay and has a partner of eleven years in El Paso. Her pastor preaches against it. She sat through Sunday sermon and could not look at anyone.

lineup.name: Dwight Pelletier
lineup.situation: Two years ago he had a vasectomy and never told his wife. She now wants a second child and has started tracking her cycle.

lineup.name: Merle Gantt
lineup.situation: A tourist tonight put beans in his bowl of Texas Red and called traditional chili 'a suggestion.' Merle is still on the porch.

lineup.name: Doyle
lineup.situation: Two weeks ago he asked Silas for his account statement and was told the credit union would mail it. Nothing has come. Today, at the Study Butte store, the clerk handed him a certified-mail slip addressed to him in care of the Albuquerque law firm that is Tierra Quieta's registered agent. It is a notice for a document he can't sign for without ID that the Wellspring holds. He did not claim it.

lineup.name: Rusty Calloway
lineup.situation: Last month he passed a pressure test on a crew's equipment after being pushed to hurry. He now believes a gauge was misread. Nothing has failed. The crew's young hand, who is a friend's son, works that rig daily.

lineup.name: Imelda Saenz
lineup.situation: Her sister-in-law, who has cared for her bedridden brother for years, told her privately she wants to put him in a care home in Odessa. The family land is in his name. Imelda stands to lose the place if costs force a sale, and she realizes she hopes the sister-in-law fails.

lineup.name: Tavo Menchaca
lineup.situation: He has been lying to his parents for a year about being enrolled; he dropped his program in spring and has been living on tips. They are driving up for his graduation party Saturday and have already paid for a cake.

lineup.name: Wilhelmina Boggs
lineup.situation: She is bursting to tell the story of the night in 1987 when a guest, a famous-in-Texas fiddle player, asked her to sit while he played a whole tune at 3 a.m. because he couldn't sleep, and she never told anyone who he was.

lineup.name: Chuy Armendariz
lineup.situation: This week on a lower canyon run he found a calf stranded on a gravel bar and spent four hours getting it across the river with a client, a retired surgeon, who then performed a tiny field fix on the calf's torn leg with a guide's first-aid kit.

lineup.name: Frances Oyelowo
lineup.situation: A year ago she began studying the sky from her porch; tonight she can name thirty-one constellations and knows the Messier list by heart, and tonight on a break she saw the Leonid meteors early.

lineup.name: Orville Peck-Lansing
lineup.situation: He believes the Chinati and Davis Mountains are the rim of a collapsed volcano and that the old-timers' stories about the ground humming after rain are the caldera settling, and that a mining company already knows.

lineup.name: Delphine Archuleta
lineup.situation: A dying patient, a rancher with no family, asked her to read him letters from a woman in Marfa he has not seen since 1974. The woman is alive and lives twenty miles away. Delphine could bring her.

lineup.name: Marcos Villareal
lineup.situation: He is furious that the Paisano Pete statue was repainted a shade he calls wrong, and has driven past it three times tonight to confirm.

lineup.name: Silas
lineup.situation: A county road crew and a surveyor Dub hired staked the disputed strip with orange flags this morning, running straight through the one spot Gerald says will hit water. Dub then filed a formal written complaint with the county about the full-moon fires, citing fire danger. Renata responded by inviting Dub to the Unbinding in a handwritten note that Silas only saw after it was delivered. Dub's reply was a photo of the note, pinned to the surveyor's stake with a roofing nail.

lineup.name: Travis Lomax
lineup.situation: He has been hauling an uneasy secret since a wellhead sign-off he thinks he rushed. Tonight the rig crew's foreman invited him to a barbecue to thank him, and he couldn't stop shaking his hand.

lineup.name: Priyanka 'Pree' Shah
lineup.situation: She rafted below Santa Elena Canyon this afternoon and a bighorn ewe and lamb swam beside her raft, close enough to hear them breathe.

lineup.name: Hap Cardenas
lineup.situation: In 1983 he turned up an intact Model T radiator cap near Marfa with a name stamped inside, and kept it in a coffee tin ever since. He finally figured out whose it was.

lineup.name: Winston Abernathy-Cole
lineup.situation: After thirty-one nights of brightness logs he is certain the Marfa Lights are tuning for a buried machine under the Mitchell Flat, and tonight their rhythm matched his earlier logs to the second.

lineup.name: Tomasa Ibarra
lineup.situation: Her son Rudy told her yesterday he is gay and has had a partner in El Paso for eleven years. Her pastor preached against it this morning and she sat through the whole sermon.

lineup.name: Dwight Pelletier
lineup.situation: He had a vasectomy two years ago and never told his wife. She now wants a second child and has begun tracking her cycle.

lineup.name: Merle Gantt
lineup.situation: A tourist put beans in his bowl of Texas Red tonight and called the traditional recipe a suggestion. Merle is still on the porch.

lineup.name: Delphine Archuleta
lineup.situation: A dying rancher with no family asked her to read him letters from a woman in Marfa he hasn't seen since 1974. The woman is alive and lives twenty miles away.

lineup.name: Orville Peck-Lansing
lineup.situation: He believes the Chinati and Davis Mountains are the rim of a collapsed volcano and that old-timers' stories of the ground humming after rain are the caldera breathing.

lineup.name: Marguerite
lineup.situation: Alvin posted the quarterly sliding-scale sheet in the Long Tent. Her line lists seven years of 'contributions' and a balance she is told she 'owes' for housing and meals. She did the math on the porch tonight: leaving would cost her about $1,100 deposit, first month, and a bus ticket, and the sheet says she is $9,400 in the hole to a nonprofit that never paid her a wage.

lineup.name: Rosendo 'Ro' Almanza
lineup.situation: Last night at 2 a.m. on a lease road he watched a coyote stand on the hood of an abandoned pumpjack truck and wait for him. He took a photo. His crew says it's a pet. He says it has been waiting there three weeks.

lineup.name: Dr. Calista Brandt
lineup.situation: She has quietly hand-dated a layer of volcanic ash in a roadcut on Highway 118 and believes the county's historical marker is wrong by about two million years.

lineup.name: Wyatt Sandoval
lineup.situation: His father, a third-generation Presidio County rancher, just found out Wyatt has been hanging gallery shows for the people the old man calls 'the Prada crowd.' Wyatt has also been sending half his pay home without saying where it comes from, because the ranch is behind on its note.

lineup.name: Ernestine 'Tina' Quillen
lineup.situation: She found a stack of love letters between two male guests from the 1940s wedged behind a bureau drawer. One was signed by a name now on a Texas courthouse plaque. She has read all of them.

lineup.name: Dale Rinehart
lineup.situation: He sold his raft company share last year to a partner, Mateo, who then died in a flash flood. Dale has been receiving Mateo's mail and found a life insurance policy naming Dale as sole beneficiary, for $250,000, which Mateo never mentioned.

lineup.name: Lupe Carrasco
lineup.situation: A man she has been secretly seeing for four months, a married sheriff's deputy, asked her tonight to lie about his whereabouts on a night when a motorcycle crash happened and he was supposedly on duty. She has the timestamp.

lineup.name: Gus Pellerin
lineup.situation: For three nights he has heard a woman's voice singing a hymn from the empty parade ground. He recorded it. The tape is blank when he plays it back.

lineup.name: Marisol 'Sol' Benavidez
lineup.situation: Her advisor offered her a funded PhD slot on the condition she move to Lubbock, and her partner of six years just got a permanent job at the hospital in Alpine.

lineup.name: Beau Tillery
lineup.situation: He has spent three years building a perfect scale model of the Terlingua ghost town out of scrap, and last week someone broke in and rearranged the buildings.

lineup.name: Doyle
lineup.situation: On the same Monday he learned the credit union account is held by Tierra Quieta Holdings and that he is not a signer, he got back to the property and found his padlock on the soap shed hanging a different direction than he leaves it. Nothing was missing. The ledger on the shelf had been squared against the edge, and he never squares it.

lineup.name: Reggie Salcido
lineup.situation: He believes a Paisano Pete billboard he painted in 1989 is still up on a ranch fence outside town and spent the weekend finding it. Tonight he found it under a wasp-nest layer of paint and discovered his own initials and a hidden joke he'd forgotten.

lineup.name: Marisela Duran
lineup.situation: A dying patient's family asked her to keep quiet that he'd signed a will leaving his ranch to a ranch hand, not his sons. She witnessed it.

lineup.name: Gordon Hux
lineup.situation: He believes he saw a lit figure walking the tracks east of town at 2 a.m., and when he went down there the ballast showed no footprints but warm spots in a line.

lineup.name: Danielle Tafoya
lineup.situation: She slept with her best friend's husband once, a year ago, and the friend just announced she's pregnant and asked Danielle to be godmother. The baby's due date lines up.

lineup.name: Clete Brannum
lineup.situation: His late wife's recipe box turned up with a card in his own handwriting from 1971 that he doesn't remember writing, a proposal he apparently never sent.

lineup.name: Tammy Ruelas
lineup.situation: A student's mother called asking her to quietly check whether her son was in a dorm; he is, with a girl, and she isn't legally allowed to say.

lineup.name: Bix Halloran
lineup.situation: A tourist asked him tonight at a Fort Stockton truck stop why he was in a frock coat, and he spent two hours explaining Fort Stockton's own 1860s history, and the tourist cried.

lineup.name: Ofelia Quiroz
lineup.situation: She forged a professor's signature to keep a scholarship, and he just offered to write her a recommendation for a Marfa residency.

lineup.name: Lester Pym
lineup.situation: He insists that every year on the first cold night the coyotes sing the same eleven notes in the same order from the same ridge, and he has transcribed them.

lineup.name: Junie
lineup.situation: Doyle took her to the Alpine library this morning and, before she went in, told her quietly that the truck has a seat whenever she wants it and that she doesn't have to name anybody. She has decided it was a kind offer about errands. She also traced her boot with a pencil stub like Luke said, and counted that it has moved two more times since October. She reports this as a measurement.

lineup.name: Darnell Pruitt
lineup.situation: His 15-year-old daughter Kayla has asked to move in with him full time from Midland. He has been the weekend dad for six years, and he knows the real reason is that she's fighting with her mom, not that she wants him. His mother told him to say yes. His girlfriend told him to say no.

lineup.name: Hollis Beckett
lineup.situation: He has spent two years trying to match the sound of the old church bell in a Marathon yard to a foundry mark. Tonight, with a flashlight, he read a casting date on the lip he's never been able to reach before.

lineup.name: Noreen Castellano
lineup.situation: A coworker, Teddy, she has trusted for years, has been pocketing leftover opioid waste from vials. She has seen it three times. He recently got engaged and told her he's finally happy. Reporting him ends his license and maybe his life; not reporting it puts patients at risk.

lineup.name: Wendell Fisk
lineup.situation: For three weeks, between 3 and 4 a.m. on his drive home on Highway 118, his radio dies and his dashboard clock jumps exactly eleven minutes forward. He has tested three cars. Last night he pulled over at the same mile marker and the clock jumped while the engine was off.

lineup.name: Fiona Ledesma
lineup.situation: Her boyfriend of two years proposed in front of a dinner party of his friends. She said yes because everyone was watching. She has the ring in a sock drawer and has not worn it for nine days.

lineup.name: Gabe Rosales
lineup.situation: Today he removed a feral hive from inside a wall of the old Lawrence Hall and found comb nearly six feet long, with honey he says tasted of creosote bloom and something like smoke.

lineup.name: Imogen Vance
lineup.situation: She has been giving a neighbor, a widowed old miner named Pascual, free meals for a year. Last week he asked her to sign a paper as witness to his will, naming her as heir to his claim and cabin. His nephews don't know she exists.

lineup.name: Lonnie Quarles
lineup.situation: On his porch tonight in the 48-degree dark he saw what he's sure was a fireball that split in three and made no sound for at least ninety seconds before a faint low rumble. He has reported it to the American Meteor Society and wants to know if anyone else saw it.

lineup.name: Sloane Whitaker
lineup.situation: She won $2,200 on a church raffle ticket her mother bought her, then drove to the casino in Presidio, stood in the parking lot for an hour, and did not go in. Tonight her roommate found the cash and thinks she lost it. She is considering telling the truth: that she didn't gamble, but wanted to.

lineup.name: Renata
lineup.situation: She is on a supply run, buying ochre-safe skin sealant, hand warmers and scorpion-proof tent stakes for the first desert Unbinding at the next full moon. A seeker backed out this morning because of the forty-degree nights, and her spreadsheet of who wears which stone color now has a blank column she can't explain. She noticed Silas's seat at the rehearsal walk-through was never going to be filled.

lineup.name: Travis Odom
lineup.situation: Three weeks ago he saw his foreman falsify a spill report to avoid a fine. The spill leaked toward a stock tank on a neighbor's ranch. The foreman paid for his daughter's quinceañera.

lineup.name: Delfina Reyes
lineup.situation: She has found out the man she's been quietly dating for a year, a widower, still wears his late wife's wedding ring on a chain, and she saw him visit the grave at the Marfa cemetery with fresh flowers on the night he told her he was working late.

lineup.name: Colt Haverty
lineup.situation: He crashed his father's truck in October, lied that a deer did it, and the insurance paid. In truth he was driving drunk and a friend, Bobby, took a concussion and never told anyone. Bobby now wants to go to the rodeo finals and the story is about to come out.

lineup.name: Nadine Whitcomb
lineup.situation: A patient's adult daughter, Paula, asked her to stay with her mother on Thanksgiving so Paula can fly home to Houston to see her kids. Nadine's own mother is in a care home in El Paso and she hasn't visited in five months.

lineup.name: Orrin Basch
lineup.situation: He spent thirty years cleaning the mirror of the 107-inch telescope and tells how once, on a night of heavy snow, he was alone on the mountain and every dome light went out at once while he stood watching the Milky Way come down to the ground like a curtain.

lineup.name: Mavis Teel
lineup.situation: Last night one of her nanny goats gave birth to triplets in a thunderless blue norther, and she spent the night in the barn singing Patsy Cline to keep the kids warm. One of them is solid black with a white star.

lineup.name: Elias Quintero
lineup.situation: He is convinced a pattern of small earthquakes registered near Alpine over the past month are the opening movements of a major fault event, and he has drawn a map in a notebook showing the fault line passing under the Sul Ross football field.

lineup.name: Gwen Alderete
lineup.situation: She tried out her first five minutes at an open mic in Marfa and bombed in front of a table of Chinati artists, then found out one of them wrote a glowing review of her anyway, calling her 'brutally good.' She doesn't know whether it's a joke or a compliment.

lineup.name: Rosario Medina
lineup.situation: Her son Danny, a Border Patrol agent, asked her tonight to stop feeding the migrants who knock at her back door, saying it could end his career. She has fed three people this month. She believes it's a moral line, and he believes it's the law.

lineup.name: Alvin
lineup.situation: Alvin was reconciling the quarter when he found a $14,000 disbursement dated September, to a fencing contractor in Presidio. It has no corresponding line in any ledger he keeps. He did not book it. Someone else's money paid off the lien, and he suspects the payment came through the entity he says is not one of theirs. His books still reconcile to the penny, but only because that line sits outside them.

lineup.name: Maribel Ochoa
lineup.situation: Her 17-year-old son's best friend, who has practically lived at her house since sixth grade, told her he is leaving for the Army in January. Her son doesn't know. The friend made her promise not to tell until after Christmas, and her son is about to spend his savings on a road trip they planned together.

lineup.name: Gil Huerta
lineup.situation: He found a ledger in his late father's toolbox. It records a hundred and twelve nights of Marfa Lights sightings from 1951 to 1953, each with a hand-drawn color. His father never said a word about it. Gil has compared it against the record in his head and found that the colors changed every winter.

lineup.name: Dax Whitfield
lineup.situation: A tipsy regular told him last Saturday that she is his half-sister, born to his father before his parents married. He has since confirmed with his father, who confirmed it flatly and asked him not to tell his mother, who has been dead nine years.

lineup.name: Concepcion 'Connie' Barraza
lineup.situation: Every December her family makes four hundred tamales in an assembly line at her kitchen table. This year her daughter announced she is buying them from a restaurant in El Paso. Connie lied that her hands hurt too much to do it, which isn't true.

lineup.name: Rafael 'Rafa' Quintanilla
lineup.situation: A client died of a heart attack on his raft in October, miles from any road. He did CPR for ninety minutes while the group watched, and the man's widow just sent him a card thanking him. He cannot get past the idea that he should have turned the raft around an hour earlier.

lineup.name: Opal Teague-Winslow
lineup.situation: She has recorded daily temperatures for twenty-two years and says tonight's 43 degrees is the exact reading she took on her wedding night in 1982. It is the eleventh time in twenty-two years that the date has matched a significant day of her life, and she has charted all of them.

lineup.name: Tuck Ballard
lineup.situation: His wife of six years told him last night that she wants to move to Midland to be near her family. He makes good money hauling water, but the work keeps him gone twenty days a month. He realizes he hasn't once asked what she wants, only what he can afford.

lineup.name: Lucinda Perea
lineup.situation: While cleaning out a courthouse annex she found a deed from 1931 that transfers a small parcel to a person named only 'the Widow Esperanza'. No surname appears anywhere, and no later record exists. She has spent three weekends in the archive trying to trace her and has now found two other deeds with the same wording.

lineup.name: Boyd Castellano
lineup.situation: He was suspended this month after a rival accused him of tasting with a stuffy nose and, worse, of favoring a cook from Alpine. He insists his nose was fine, his scoring was sound, and that the rival had added a forbidden dash of cinnamon.
